Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves that later turn dark and scabby; fruit gets rough, cracked scab-like patches.
Apple___Apple_scab.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis.

severity.Mild: A few small spots on young leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, some leaves yellowing and curling, scabs on a few fruits.
severity.Severe: Most leaves spotted and dropping early, fruit badly scabbed and cracked.

Apple___Apple_scab.spread: Spores survive in fallen leaves over winter and spread by wind and rain in cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Rake and remove fallen leaves in autumn, prune for good air flow, and choose scab-resistant varieties.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown leaf spots with a purple edge ('frogeye'), black rotting fruit, and rough, cracked cankers on branches.
Apple___Black_rot.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa.

severity.Mild: A few frogeye spots on leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many leaf spots, some fruit starting to rot.
severity.Severe: Fruit rotted and mummified, branches with cankers, heavy leaf loss.

Apple___Black_rot.spread: Spores come from dead wood, cankers and mummified fruit, and spread by rain splash and wind.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions. Prune out cankered branches.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified fruit and dead wood, prune in dry weather, and keep trees healthy and well fed.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface, with small tube-like growths underneath; fruit may be deformed.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae, which needs both apple and juniper/cedar trees.

severity.Mild: A few yellow-orange spots on leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, leaves yellowing, some fruit affected.
severity.Severe: Heavy leaf spotting and early leaf drop, weak tree, distorted fruit.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.spread: Spores travel by wind between nearby juniper/cedar trees and apple trees in wet spring weather.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby juniper or cedar hosts if possible, plant resistant apple varieties, and apply protective sprays at the right time.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves, leaf curling and distortion; fruit can be affected.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Podosphaera clandestina.

severity.Mild: Small white patches on a few leaves.
severity.Moderate: White coating on many leaves, some curling.
severity.Severe: Most leaves covered and distorted, fruit affected, growth stunted.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.spread: Spores spread by wind; favoured by warm days, cool nights and crowded, shaded growth.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Prune for air flow, avoid too much nitrogen fertiliser, and plant in sunny, open spots.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular tan to grey lesions that run parallel to the leaf veins.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis.

severity.Mild: A few lesions on lower leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many lesions, spreading to middle leaves.
severity.Severe: Lesions join together, upper leaves killed, yield drops.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.spread: Spores survive in crop residue and spread by wind and rain; worse in warm, humid weather and with maize after maize.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Rotate crops, bury or remove residue, choose tolerant hybrids, and avoid very dense planting.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, round to oval, reddish-brown powdery pustules on both sides of the leaf.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi.

severity.Mild: A few pustules on some leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many pustules across the leaves.
severity.Severe: Leaves covered, turning yellow and drying out early.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.spread: Spores are carried long distances by wind; cool, moist weather favours the disease.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, sow on time, and monitor fields early.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on the leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Exserohilum turcicum.

severity.Mild: A few lesions on lower leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many lesions reaching the middle leaves.
severity.Severe: Large lesions join up, leaves die early, yield loss.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.spread: Spores survive on crop residue and spread by wind and rain in moderate temperatures and humid weather.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Rotate crops, manage residue, and plant resistant hybrids.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with tiny black dots; berries turn brown, then shrivel into hard black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Guignardia bidwellii.

severity.Mild: A few leaf spots.
severity.Moderate: Many leaf spots, some berries starting to rot.
severity.Severe: Most berries shrivelled and black, heavy loss of crop.

Grape___Black_rot.spread: Spores survive in mummified berries and old canes and spread by rain in warm, wet weather.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected canes, prune for air flow, and spray protectively before and after flowering.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow and brown patterns between leaf veins, dark spots on berries, and decayed wood inside the vine.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).type_cause: Fungal disease complex (including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora) that rots the vine's wood.

severity.Mild: A few leaves with stripes.
severity.Moderate: Stripes on many leaves, some berries spotted.
severity.Severe: Whole shoots or vines wilt suddenly, berries shrivel, vine may die.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).spread: Spores enter through pruning wounds and spread by wind and rain.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: There is no full cure. Cut out and burn infected wood, and protect pruning wounds. Ask a local expert about wound treatments.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Prune in dry weather, disinfect tools, protect wounds, and avoid injuring vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Dark brown, angular spots on leaves, which can join together and cause early leaf drop.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Pseudocercospora vitis (Isariopsis).

severity.Mild: A few small spots.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, some leaves yellowing.
severity.Severe: Most leaves spotted, early defoliation, weak fruit ripening.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.spread: Spores spread by wind and rain in warm, humid weather.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Remove fallen leaves, prune for air flow, and avoid overhead watering.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy yellow mottling on leaves, small lopsided bitter fruit that stays green at the bottom, twig dieback.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).type_cause: Bacterial disease caused by Candidatus Liberibacter, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect.

severity.Mild: A few shoots with yellow blotchy leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many branches affected, fruit small and misshapen.
severity.Severe: Whole tree declines, heavy fruit drop, tree eventually dies.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).spread: Spread mainly by the psyllid insect feeding on leaves, and by infected plants and grafts.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: There is no cure. Remove infected trees as advised by local authorities and control the psyllid insect.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Buy certified disease-free plants, monitor and control psyllids, and report suspected cases to the agriculture department.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular water-soaked spots on leaves that turn purple-brown and fall out ('shot-hole'); fruit gets pitted, cracked spots.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.type_cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni.

severity.Mild: A few small spots on leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, shot-holes forming, yellowing leaves.
severity.Severe: Heavy leaf drop, fruit pitted and cracked.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.spread: Spreads by wind-driven rain and survives on twigs and buds over winter.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves or plants and avoid working in the field when plants are wet. Copper-based sprays are commonly used to slow bacterial diseases; confirm the right product with a local agriculture officer.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant tolerant varieties, avoid overhead watering, keep trees well nourished, and prune for air flow.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn brown with a yellow halo; raised, scabby spots on fruit.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.type_cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas species.

severity.Mild: A few spots on leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, leaves yellowing and dropping.
severity.Severe: Heavy leaf drop, fruit scabbed and sun-scalded, big yield loss.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.spread: Seed-borne and spread by rain splash, wind, tools and workers handling wet plants.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves or plants and avoid working in the field when plants are wet. Copper-based sprays are commonly used to slow bacterial diseases; confirm the right product with a local agriculture officer.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use clean certified seed, rotate crops, avoid overhead watering, and sanitise tools.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with rings like a target on older leaves, with yellowing around them.
Potato___Early_blight.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani.

severity.Mild: A few spots on lower leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, yellowing and some leaf drop.
severity.Severe: Most leaves dead, stems and tubers affected, yield drops.

Potato___Early_blight.spread: Spores spread by wind, rain splash and tools; favoured by warm, humid weather and stressed plants.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, use healthy seed tubers, water the soil rather than the leaves, and keep plants well fed.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark, water-soaked patches on leaves, with white fuzzy growth underneath in damp weather; tubers rot.
Potato___Late_blight.type_cause: Water mold (oomycete) disease caused by Phytophthora infestans.

severity.Mild: A few dark patches on leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many patches, spreading to stems.
severity.Severe: Whole plant collapses within days and tubers rot.

Potato___Late_blight.spread: Spores spread quickly by wind and rain in cool, wet weather and from infected tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions. Act quickly; this disease spreads very fast.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified seed tubers, destroy volunteer plants and cull piles, and monitor closely in wet weather.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on the upper surface of leaves, which can cover the whole leaf and make it turn yellow and dry.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Podosphaera xanthii.

severity.Mild: A few white patches on older leaves.
severity.Moderate: White coating on many leaves.
severity.Severe: Leaves fully covered, yellow and dying, fruit smaller.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.spread: Spores spread by wind; warm days, humid air and crowded plants favour it.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Give plants space, choose resistant varieties, water at the base, and remove badly infected leaves.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small purple spots on leaves, which enlarge and give a scorched look as the centres turn brown.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Diplocarpon earlianum.

severity.Mild: A few small purple spots.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, some leaves turning brown.
severity.Severe: Leaves scorched and dying, plant weakened, lower yield.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.spread: Spores survive on old leaves and spread by rain splash.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Remove old infected leaves, avoid overhead watering, space plants well, and use resistant varieties.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves with a yellow halo; small raised scabby spots on fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.type_cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas species.

severity.Mild: A few small spots.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, leaves yellowing and dropping.
severity.Severe: Heavy defoliation and fruit covered with scabs.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.spread: Seed-borne and spread by rain splash, wind and tools in warm, wet weather.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves or plants and avoid working in the field when plants are wet. Copper-based sprays are commonly used to slow bacterial diseases; confirm the right product with a local agriculture officer.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use clean seed, rotate crops, avoid overhead watering, and avoid handling wet plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (like a target) on older leaves, with yellowing around them.
Tomato___Early_blight.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani.

severity.Mild: A few spots on lower leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, yellowing, some leaves dying.
severity.Severe: Most leaves lost, stems and fruit spotted, yield drops.

Tomato___Early_blight.spread: Spores spread by wind, rain splash and tools; favoured by warm, humid weather.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, use drip irrigation, space and stake plants, and mulch around the base.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large dark, water-soaked patches on leaves and stems, white fuzzy growth underneath in damp weather, brown firm rot on fruit.
Tomato___Late_blight.type_cause: Water mold (oomycete) disease caused by Phytophthora infestans.

severity.Mild: A few dark patches on leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many patches spreading to stems.
severity.Severe: Plants collapse quickly and fruit rots.

Tomato___Late_blight.spread: Spores spread rapidly by wind and rain in cool, wet weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions. Act quickly; this disease spreads very fast.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid overhead watering, space plants, and remove infected plants at once.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green-yellow spots on the upper leaf surface with olive-grey velvety mold underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Passalora fulva.

severity.Mild: A few spots on lower leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, leaves curling and yellowing.
severity.Severe: Most leaves dry and fall off, fruit exposed and yield drops.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.spread: Spores spread by air, water and tools; common in humid, poorly ventilated places such as greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Improve ventilation, lower humidity, avoid wetting leaves, and use resistant varieties.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey centres (with tiny black dots), mostly on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici.

severity.Mild: A few spots on lower leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, leaves yellowing and dying from the bottom up.
severity.Severe: Heavy leaf loss, fruit exposed to sunscald.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.spread: Spores survive on crop residue and spread by rain splash, tools and hands in warm, wet weather.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate crops, remove plant debris, mulch, and water at the base of the plant.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Tiny pale speckles on leaves that turn yellow or bronze, fine webbing underneath, and dry, curled leaves.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.type_cause: Pest damage caused by the two-spotted spider mite (Tetranychus urticae), a tiny sap-sucking mite rather than a germ.

severity.Mild: A few speckled leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many leaves speckled and yellowing, light webbing.
severity.Severe: Leaves dry and drop, heavy webbing, plant weak.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.spread: Mites multiply fast in hot, dry weather and spread by wind, on clothes and on infested plants.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Spray plants firmly with water, use insecticidal soap or oil, or a miticide approved in your area. Ask a local agriculture officer.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Keep plants watered and not dusty, check the underside of leaves regularly, and protect natural predators of mites.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings and a yellow edge on leaves; spots can also appear on stems and fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.type_cause: Fungal disease caused by Corynespora cassiicola.

severity.Mild: A few spots on lower leaves.
severity.Moderate: Many spots, leaves yellowing.
severity.Severe: Heavy leaf drop and spotted, sunburned fruit.

Tomato___Target_Spot.spread: Spores spread by wind and rain; warm, humid weather favours it.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves or plants. Use a fungicide that is approved for this crop in your area, following the label. Ask a local agriculture officer or extension worker which product and timing suit your conditions.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Rotate crops, space plants for air flow, remove plant debris, and avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward and turn yellow at the edges, plants are stunted and bushy, and flowers and fruit drop.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.type_cause: Viral disease (a begomovirus) spread by whiteflies.

severity.Mild: A few new leaves slightly curled.
severity.Moderate: Many leaves curled and yellow, growth slowed.
severity.Severe: Plants badly stunted with almost no fruit.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.spread: Spread by whiteflies feeding on infected then healthy plants; not spread by touch.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: There is no cure for plant viruses. Remove and destroy infected plants early, control the insects that carry the virus, and replant with healthy, certified seedlings.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Control whiteflies, use fine insect nets or resistant varieties, and remove weeds around the field.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, leaves narrow or distorted, and uneven fruit ripening.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.type_cause: Viral disease caused by Tomato mosaic virus.

severity.Mild: Slight mottling on a few leaves.
severity.Moderate: Clear mosaic and distortion on many leaves.
severity.Severe: Plants stunted, leaves badly twisted, low fruit yield.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.spread: Spreads by touch (hands and tools), infected seed and plant debris; the virus survives for a long time.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: There is no cure for plant viruses. Remove and destroy infected plants early, control the insects that carry the virus, and replant with healthy, certified seedlings.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use clean seed, wash hands and disinfect tools, do not smoke or touch plants after tobacco, and remove infected plants.
